timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only CLI stream with no projected semantic events; accounted in manifest but not used for event reasoning.
Parent trajectory probes the binary, writes Rust implementation, fuzzes locally, launches the large verifier workflow, edits parse handling, and then times out.
Negative-input verifier child reads sources, runs negative fuzzing, finds subnormal boundary issues, and is interrupted before a returned workflow result.
Tie-case verifier child runs ties fuzzing, hand-probes equal-channel and subnormal cases, and is interrupted with no parent-visible workflow return.
Extreme-value verifier child runs extreme/hex/boundary fuzzing and reports parse and NaN-sign mismatches before interruption.
String-parsing verifier child probes spellings, subnormals, non-UTF8 bytes, and observes source/binary inconsistency while parent edits.
Mixed-input retry child runs mixed fuzzing and notices source consistency problems near the timeout.
Initial mixed-input child runs assigned mixed fuzzing and targeted formatter probes before being interrupted.
Initial tiny-input child fuzzes tiny values and identifies exact hex subnormal behavior before interruption.
Huge-value verifier child runs huge fuzzing and formatter/overflow probes but does not return an aggregate workflow result.
Special-value verifier child performs NaN and subnormal sweeps, confirms mismatches, and is interrupted before parent consumption.
Initial hue verifier child runs hue fuzzing and disassembles the C++ binary to audit hue branch details before interruption.
Hue retry verifier child repeats hue fuzzing, examines source and disassembly, and is interrupted without parent handoff.
Tiny retry verifier child probes exact subnormal hex literals and glibc strtof behavior before interruption.
Uniform verifier child runs broad uniform, grid, pair-equal, and formatter sweeps with no mismatches before interruption.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the Rust 2021, std-only, Cargo project, root test20.rs, black-box behavior, command-line parsing, byte-identical formatting, and output executable requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and local differential testing; after producing a candidate, it delegated broad adversarial verification to a workflow with ten initial fuzz children plus planned audits.
parallel.implementation: Implemented modular Rust under /output with color conversion, ostream formatting, stof parsing, and test20.rs; fixed hue storage, saturation, NaN propagation, non-UTF8 handling, and subnormal parsing issues.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent wrote /output/Cargo.toml, /output/test20.rs, src modules, and a compiled /output/test20; artifact validation copied the expected entry and library files successfully.
parallel.verification: Parent ran examples and differential fuzzing before launching the workflow; children performed additional fuzz/audit probes, but the workflow was killed before a consolidated result returned.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official artifact passed 40/40, but the agent process timed out, final.txt is empty, and the parallel verifier workflow ended killed with null result.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, root test20.rs, Cargo, black-box reverse-engineering, CLI, formatting, and byte-identical output obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery without delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: Built a modular Rust port under /output/color, fixed hue normalization, saturation branch, unclamped saturation output, stof range handling, and formatter behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Created Cargo.toml, test20.rs, color modules, Cargo.lock/target artifacts, and a rebuilt executable; final artifact validation accepted the expected files.
serial.verification: Ran documented examples, local fuzzers comparing stdout/stderr/status, formatter boundary tests, Cargo release build, and a final clean rustc rebuild before responding.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official artifact passed 40/40 and the process returned normally; final response notes only a literal NaN sign-bit caveat judged unreachable from numeric arguments.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt's Rust 2021, std-only, byte-identical output, Cargo, root test20.rs, and black-box constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task obligations and explicitly reported the delivered Cargo project and byte-identical behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference affected the official outcome; both completed the required artifact, while serial also produced a final summary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent owned implementation, then delegated broad verification to a workflow with ten fuzz agents and planned audits/critic stages.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept implementation, verification, build, and final reporting in one actor with no delegation tools enabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The useful work split differed only after implementation: parallel fanned out verification, while serial stayed monolithic and completed closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verifier child briefs had detailed program shape and rules, but they read the live /output workspace while the parent kept editing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interface and locally reconciled source, binary, and verification state before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a live-workspace verifier interface, creating stale/mid-edit observations, while serial avoided cross-agent context transfer entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote src/color modules, parse/format helpers, and test20.rs, then fixed hue, NaN, non-UTF8, and subnormal behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote color modules in a flatter /output/color layout and converged through local experiments on the same mathematical and formatting details.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Implementation layouts differed, but both implemented the required behavior well enough for the official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel's verifier workflow remained backgrounded, was killed with null result, and the parent final response is empty.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a normal assistant end-turn with a final validation summary after local checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the verifier aggregate and final communication lifecycle to timeout; serial delivered a complete closure narrative.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent and verifier children shared the live /output tree; children inspected /output while parent edits and rebuild attempts were still happening.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial alone wrote and rebuilt /output, then listed the final deliverables and executable after a clean rebuild.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-state exposure during verification, but no proven live overwrite or write collision changed the final passing artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had local fuzz success and examples before workflow launch, then an unfinished workflow; official evaluator passed all 40 testcases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed local examples, broad fuzzing, formatter tests, Cargo and rustc builds, then official evaluator passed all 40 testcases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both passed official acceptance, but serial's pre-closure verification was completed and reported while parallel's workflow verification was not joined.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full 2399-second agent budget and exited with returncode 143 after the verifier workflow remained active.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial returned code 0 after 2331 seconds, with remaining budget and a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Budget closure is the main difference: parallel timed out post-implementation, while serial closed normally.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial pass 40/40. The concrete task-solving difference is that parallel reached a passing artifact but spent the remaining budget on a broad verifier workflow that was killed and left no final response, whereas serial performed comparable reverse-engineering and verification locally, returned normally, and documented validation. This does not explain an official outcome gap because there is no official gap.

serial_contributors: Single actor retained ownership of implementation, verification, and final response
Local rustc, Cargo, examples, fuzzing, and formatter checks completed before closure
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a src/color module layout while serial used a /output/color module layout
Both independently converged on hue normalization, saturation branch, ostream formatting, and stof edge behavior
